transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, is it okay if I just sit right here? Great, thanks. 

Well, I guess I'm here because... I've been feeling a little stressed lately? I mean, I know everyone gets stressed, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything. I have a good job in tech and a great family. But I just... I can't seem to stop worrying about kind of everything at once. I hope that doesn't sound too ridiculous. 

It's just this constant loop about my marriage, and whether I'm slipping up at work... um, bills, the house projects I keep dropping. And I guess, if I'm being completely honest—and I feel really embarrassed even admitting this out loud—I just worry all the time that I'm basically failing as a husband and a father. 

Does... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining this the right way for you.
Have you been avoiding any activities or situations because of your worries?

No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still go to work every day, and I'm there for my family. I wouldn't want to let anyone down by just... not showing up, you know? 

I guess sometimes I might put off looking at the bank account for a few days, or I'll wait to reply to an email if I'm not totally sure I have the perfect answer... but that's just normal procrastination, right? I'm not really avoiding anything major. I try really hard to keep up with everything. Is that the kind of thing you meant?
Have you noticed any changes in your physical health, such as headaches or difficulty sleeping, since you started feeling this way?

Um, physically I think I'm mostly okay. I really try to take care of myself, so I don't want to sound like a hypochondriac or anything. I don't really get bad headaches. But, um... I guess my sleep hasn't been great lately? I mean, I know a lot of busy people struggle with sleep, so I'm sure it's nothing out of the ordinary. 

It's just... most nights I'll lie in bed, and I am completely exhausted, but my brain just keeps running. I end up going over all the project risks at work, or money stuff, or overthinking something I said to my wife earlier. And then, even when I do finally manage to fall asleep, I almost always wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning. And I just can't get back down after that, because I'm already lying there rehearsing all of tomorrow's problems in my head. 

I'm sorry, I know that's a lot of complaining. Is... is it pretty normal for stress to mess with your sleep like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

No, no, I wouldn't say I'm sad. I mean, I have so much to be grateful for, you know? A great job, a beautiful family... I'd feel terrible complaining about being sad when I have it so good. 

I don't really feel down, exactly. It's more just... I feel like I'm constantly running on a treadmill that's going a little too fast. It's just the worrying and the stress that gets to me, not really sadness. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude for my wife and kids. I hope that's the right answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm ungrateful for my life or anything.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or anxiety that reached a peak within minutes?

Oh, um, no. No, I don't think I've ever had anything quite like that. 

Like I was saying, I try really hard to keep things together, especially at work or around my family. It's never really a sudden... explosion of fear out of nowhere. It's more just that constant, steady hum of stress all day long. I've never had one of those moments where I felt like I couldn't breathe or needed to rush to the hospital or anything dramatic. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to be clear that I'm still functioning and not, you know, completely losing control. I'm really trying my best to manage it. Is that the kind of distinction you were looking for?
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to repeat over and over in your mind?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I definitely overthink things, like I mentioned with work and stuff, but it's not like... I don't have weird urges or anything like that. 

I'm just a bit of a perfectionist, I guess? I always want to make sure I'm doing a good job and not letting anyone down. So I might double-check an email before I send it, or run through a presentation a few times in my head, just to be safe. But it's all just normal work stuff. I don't have any strange thoughts that I can't get rid of or anything that would make me seem, you know, crazy. 

I'm completely in control of my thoughts, I promise. It's just the everyday stress that gets a little overwhelming sometimes. Does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you worry about being judged or evaluated by others in social situations?

Um, no... I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm actually pretty comfortable around people. I go to team lunches and, you know, talk with the other guys at the office without feeling like everyone is secretly evaluating me or anything. 

I always try to be really friendly and easy to work with, and I get along great with my colleagues. It's really just the work itself—making sure everything is perfect and I'm not dropping the ball on my projects—that's what gets my gears turning. Not the social part. 

I hope that's a good sign? I definitely enjoy being around my friends and family, and I don't really have any trouble talking to people. I just want to make sure I'm answering this right for you. Is that what you were asking about?
Do you have any thoughts that keep coming back to you, even when you try to ignore them or think about something else?

Well, um... I guess if we're talking about, like, everyday responsibilities... maybe a little bit? But I really think it just shows how much I care about my job and my family, you know? 

Like, sometimes, even when I tell myself to just focus on the code right in front of me, or... or if I'm trying to just breathe through a workout and clear my head... it's hard to turn the planning off completely. It's not weird thoughts, just... one concern sort of hooks onto another. And then suddenly I'm twenty steps ahead, imagining a bad review turning into losing my job, and then I'm worrying about my family being worse off because of me. 

I do try to push it away and focus on other things, but it's tricky sometimes. But I mean, any good provider worries about those kinds of things, right? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is. I just want to be thorough for you. Does that make sense for what you were asking?
Are there any specific situations or topics that you find yourself worrying about more than others?

Um, well... it's kind of a lot of things, to be honest. I guess that's sort of why I decided to come in. It's not just one specific thing, it's more like... everything at once? 

I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I have a good life, but I just can't seem to stop worrying about... well, my marriage, for one. And then I start thinking about work, like I mentioned, and whether my performance is slipping. And then that bleeds into worrying about the bills, and... oh, all those house projects I started and just keep dropping because I can't focus. 

It just feels like I'm constantly worried that I'm basically failing as a husband and a father. I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic, and I really do try to keep it together for them. I just want to be the best I can be for my family. Is it normal to have all those things piling up at once? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Is there one area of your life where you feel your worrying is most prominent?

Um, well... I guess if I had to pick just one area... it's kind of hard because it all sort of blends together, you know? Like I said, it's work, it's my marriage, it's the house... 

I wouldn't say there's one thing that stands out as, like, the absolute worst. I mean, I really try to stay on top of everything, and I think I do a decent job most of the time. It's just that the worry sort of... bounces around from one thing to the next. Like, if I get a handle on work, then I start stressing about whether I'm spending enough quality time with my wife, and if I focus on her, I worry I'm falling behind on the bills. 

So... no, not really one specific area. It's more of a general feeling, I guess? I hope that's an okay answer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can figure this out. Does that make sense?
Is your worrying more focused on your work life or your personal life?

Um... honestly, I think it's pretty much an even split? I wish I could give you a more clear-cut answer, I really do. I know I kind of just touched on this, and I don't want to make your job harder by being vague... it's just that they really seem to feed into each other. 

If I'm at work, I'm stressing about personal stuff, and if I'm home, I'm stressing about work. I try my absolute best to keep them separate so I don't, you know, burden my wife with office politics or let my family stuff affect my code... but the worrying itself is just kind of... everywhere equally? 

I hope that's an okay answer. I just don't want to mislead you by picking one if it's not actually true. Am I making sense with how I'm explaining this?
Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your ability to enjoy daily activities or causing significant distress for you?

Um... well, I really try not to let it get to me, you know? I want to be someone who just handles things well and doesn't let the stress show. But... if I'm being completely honest, and I really hate to even admit this because I feel like I should be doing better... it is starting to sort of get in the way. 

Like, at work, I've been so in my head that my manager actually started documenting some missed architectural details in my designs. Which is incredibly embarrassing, because I usually pride myself on being really thorough and reliable for the team. And at home... I know I mentioned the house projects earlier, but I just keep leaving them half-finished. I'm just showing up so distracted lately that my wife and I... well, the arguments have been escalating a bit. 

I really don't want to be a burden on her, or on my boss, and I'm trying my absolute best to fix it. I hope I don't sound like I'm just complaining or making excuses. Is that the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?

Um... well, I really try to keep my composure, you know? I don't want to be someone who makes other people nervous by fidgeting all the time or acting jumpy. But... yeah, if I'm being completely honest, I guess I do feel pretty on edge. 

I actually feel kind of wound tight almost all day. It's a little embarrassing to admit, because I feel like a grown man should be able to just relax, but my shoulders just feel completely locked up. It's like I'm constantly bracing for something to happen. I try my absolute best to hide it, but I keep catching myself pacing back and forth between my meetings at work. And even when I'm supposed to be unwinding, like at my chess club, I'm just constantly tapping the pieces. 

It's just that sitting still feels almost impossible right now, no matter how hard I try to force myself to just chill out. I really hope I'm not coming across as too intense or... or neurotic. I know I should just be able to take a deep breath and settle down. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
Do you have any thoughts that feel intrusive or unwanted, and that you try to suppress or ignore?

Um... intrusive thoughts? Like... like bad thoughts? 

Well, I really try to keep my mind focused on positive things, you know? I don't want to be the kind of person who dwells on dark or weird stuff. I think... I think my thoughts are mostly just normal worrying, like I mentioned before. Just the usual stress about work deadlines and the house projects and not wanting to let anyone down. 

I don't really have thoughts that pop into my head that feel completely out of left field or... or inappropriate, if that's what you mean. It's more just a constant stream of "did I do this right?" and "what if I mess this up?" rather than anything I feel like I have to actively suppress. I just try to push through the stress and keep working. 

Is that... is that normal? I hope I'm understanding the question right. I just want to make sure I'm not missing something you're looking for.
Have you ever experienced a sudden, intense fear or discomfort that peaks within minutes and includes symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

Um... a sudden, intense fear? Like a panic attack, you mean? 

Well, I really try to keep things under control. I know a lot of people struggle with those, and I don't want to sound like I'm making a big deal out of nothing. I mean, sure, sometimes when the pressure at work gets really high, or I realize I've messed up a detail on a design, my heart might beat a little faster. But I think that's pretty normal, right? Just a regular reaction to stress. 

I don't think I've ever had a moment where it just... peaks out of nowhere and I can't breathe or anything extreme like that. I usually just try to take a breath, get a glass of water, and power through it so I don't alarm my coworkers or my wife. I really try to handle it before it gets to that point. 

I hope that makes sense. Is it okay that I don't have those? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Is there a particular part of your life where you feel your worrying is most intense?

Um... a particular part of my life? 

Well, I really try to balance everything out, you know? I want to be a good employee, a good husband, a good friend... I don't want to let any one area slip. I guess... I guess if I had to pick, maybe work? But honestly, it's not just work. It's kind of... everything. 

I mean, I'll be at the office worrying about a software update, and then I'll come home and worry that I didn't mow the lawn exactly right, or that I said something awkward to a neighbor. It just sort of bleeds into all of it. I try to keep it compartmentalized, I really do, because I know it's probably annoying for my wife if I'm always stressing about little things around the house when I should just be relaxing with her. 

So I wouldn't say there's one specific area that's worse than the others. It's just... a general feeling that I need to stay on top of everything so nothing falls apart. I hope that's an okay answer. Does that help, or did you need me to narrow it down more? I can try to think of a specific example if you want.
Are you finding it harder to meet your responsibilities at work or at home because of your worrying?

Um... harder to meet my responsibilities? 

Well, I really try my absolute best to keep everything running smoothly, you know? I want to be reliable. I don't want to be the guy making excuses. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has been a little tough lately. I hate to even admit this, because I really pride myself on my work, but... my manager has actually started documenting some missed architectural details on my recent software projects. I'm sure he's just doing his job and being thorough, but it feels terrible because I really want to do good work for them. I'm trying so hard to get back on track so he doesn't think less of me. 

And then at home... well, I feel awful about this too, but I've been leaving a lot of house projects half-finished. I just get so wrapped up in my head and distracted by everything I'm stressing over, and I know it's incredibly unfair to my wife. I'm showing up so distracted that we've been getting into arguments, and they just... they keep escalating lately. Which isn't like us at all. I really want to be a good husband, and I'm trying to fix it so she's not so frustrated with me. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope it's okay that I shared all that. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right and not sounding like a terrible employee or anything.
Are you finding it harder to enjoy time with your family or friends because of your worrying?

Um... harder to enjoy time with family or friends? 

Well, I try really hard to be present, you know? I want to be a good friend, and I definitely want to be good company when we do get together. I wouldn't say I'm not enjoying them... I mean, I love my friends and family. They're great. 

I guess sometimes I might be a little quiet or, um, maybe a bit preoccupied in my head when we're hanging out. But I always make sure to smile and nod and ask them how they're doing. I don't want to bring anyone down or ruin the mood with my own stuff. I really make an effort to keep things light and positive for them. 

So, I don't think it's ruining my enjoyment, exactly. I just... maybe I'm not always the life of the party right now. But I'm still showing up and trying my best to be a good guy to be around. Is that... is that normal? I hope that answers your question okay. I just don't want it to sound like I don't care about the people in my life, because I really, really do.
Are you finding it harder to concentrate at work or complete tasks because of your worrying?

Um... harder to concentrate at work? 

Well, I always try to give my job a hundred percent, you know? I'm really lucky to have my position, and I definitely don't want to come across as slacking or anything. I try to stay focused. 

But... I guess if I'm being totally honest, there are moments where it's a little tricky. Like, um, during sprint planning or when we're doing code reviews. I'll catch myself reading the same design note, like, three or four times. And I still end up missing some of the details. It's just... part of my mind is off calculating what I might have forgotten to do at home, or I'm worrying about how badly the next argument with my wife is going to go. 

I really try to snap out of it quickly, though. I don't want to hold up the team or make anyone think I'm not dedicated. I just... I get a little distracted sometimes. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I don't sound like a terrible employee for admitting that. I really am trying my best to stay on top of things.
Do you often feel like you can't sit still and need to be moving or doing something?

Um... feeling like I can't sit still? 

Well, I try really hard to be calm and collected, especially around the office or when I'm out with people. I don't want to be disruptive or make anyone else feel anxious just by being around me, you know? I really try to keep it together.

But... I guess, yeah, sitting completely still is... it's a little tough for me right now. I just feel kind of, um, wound tight almost all day. Like my shoulders are just locked up and I'm constantly bracing for something to happen. I try to hide it, but I do catch myself pacing around the house, or even pacing in the hallway between my meetings at work. And, um, I go to this chess club, and I've noticed I'm always tapping the pieces when it's not my turn. I try to stop as soon as I realize I'm doing it because I don't want to annoy the other players, but sitting still just feels... almost impossible sometimes. 

Is that... is that the kind of restlessness you mean? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm completely out of control or anything. I really do try my best to sit quietly when I need to.
